what: Academy Sports + Outdoors is a sporting goods retailer with around 300 large-format stores, mainly in Texas and the southern United States. It sells sporting equipment, outdoor and hunting gear, fishing supplies, apparel, footwear and summer seasonal goods, combining national brands with its own value-priced labels. Its fiscal year ends around the end of January.
customers: Value-conscious families in the South and Southeast buying sports, outdoor, hunting and fishing gear, clothing and footwear.
money: Hunting, fishing, camping, firearms and ammunition, and patio and grills.
National brands like Nike and own brands.
Team sports, fitness equipment, bikes and summer gear.
moat: Academy’s advantage is its regional focus and value positioning in hunting and fishing, categories where it has deep assortments and loyal customers. Low-cost locations and private labels let it undercut department stores and specialty shops. Its moat is moderate, since retail is competitive and Dick’s, Walmart and online sellers sell many of the same items.
risks: Comparable sales fell for several years after the pandemic boom, with revenue sliding from $6.8B in fiscal 2022 to $5.9B in fiscal 2025.
Net income has fallen from $671M to $377M in fiscal 2026 as margins normalised.
Firearms and ammunition demand is volatile and politically sensitive.
Lower-income customers are pressured by inflation and higher interest rates.
Debt of about $2B includes significant lease obligations.
opportunities: New stores in fast-growing southern states give it room to expand outside its core.
Buybacks reduced the share count from 94M to 68M in four years.
The shares trade at about 12 times trailing and 10 times forward earnings.
Revenue has started growing again, to $6.2B over the last twelve months.
watch: Comparable sales trends, new store productivity, gross margin, firearms demand and the pace of buybacks.
view: Academy is a retailer that over-earned during the pandemic and has spent four years coming back to earth. Net income peaked at $671M in fiscal 2022 and fell to $377M in fiscal 2026 as comparable sales and margins normalised. Management used the cash wisely, cutting the share count by almost 30%, so earnings per share fell much less than net income.

The market now values it at around 12 times trailing earnings, which is roughly where good regional retailers trade when growth is slow. The new store programme into fast-growing southern markets is the main lever, and revenue over the last twelve months has turned up to $6.2B. Free cash flow has been squeezed by store-opening capex, falling from $597M to $222M, which is the price of growth.

The investment turns on whether the new stores reach the productivity of older ones, because that determines whether capex is creating value. If they do, Academy is cheap at 10 times forward earnings with a long runway of buybacks. If not, it is a fairly priced regional retailer exposed to the consumer cycle. I lean slightly positive, but this is a business to own at a discount, which it currently is.
bull: New stores ramp well, comparable sales recover and buybacks drive strong earnings-per-share growth.
bear: Consumer weakness and competition keep sales flat while new stores dilute returns.
